brief: GS TMT sales note: US equities had a rough week on hot inflation, higher oil and AI-trade worries. Semis fell an 8th session, memory weakened, and momentum unwound; hedge funds cut net exposure almost entirely via new shorts, not fewer longs, with long/short funds down 2.7% and record IT net selling. VIX futures traded 3.6x their 20-day average, GS's first real sign of index-protection panic after weeks of single-stock damage. The bigger development, per GS, is credit: AI-linked spreads widened for neoclouds and AI-lab-exposed names, which fell ~25% on the week, while Microsoft reportedly backs away from a neocloud deal. GS frames the debate as shifting from how fast AI capex grows to who funds it and where returns accrue; capex may be past peak, and credit quality/ROIC now weigh on equity valuations, with earnings season the key test. AI Hyperscaler Equities (GSXUHYPR) were 15% lower the last time spreads were this wide. Separately, Nvidia is pushing memory makers toward TSMC's 3nm for HBM dies; OpenAI's CFO says contracted compute could resell 3-5x above contract value, cited as a sign external AI financing is nearing its peak. The note also previews this week's TMT earnings: SAP, Meta, TXN, BESI, telcos, Pearson, RELX, Spotify, TSMC and Japan electronics.
